causal_findings.summary: The1789 year entry makes readers scan unrelated constitutional, economic, church and international treatments. The destinations remain readable and thematic routes elsewhere retrieve those facts. Missing topical selectors delay selection; no evidence establishes that the year architecture itself falsely characterizes a treatment or blocks it. Its length does not justify major.

Constitution, church conflict, Varennes and foreign/colonial matters are meaningful choices hidden inside1791. A date-first reader can still inspect the listed pages and use those subject routes. The independently established harm is repeat scanning across a heterogeneous sequence, not a misleading chronological assertion or destroyed access.

War/annexation, domestic emergency, royalism and social consequences require different topical selections within1793. The needed pages and ordinary subject entries remain available; wrong-year locator errors are expressly excluded from this SUB cause. Repairable navigation friction is the supported consequence.

Army reorganization, Terror overthrow, royalist resistance and later consequences make1794 need useful subdivisions. The evidence establishes extra scanning, while those topics retain their ordinary access routes. It does not show this year label blocks or materially misleads retrieval independently of locator errors.

The1795 entry combines diplomacy, Thermidorian change, expeditions and Directory settlement. Readers lack topical selectors but retain both the date destinations and specific subject access. The inconvenience is a repairable selection burden; neither long range nor number of topics alone supplies a major consequence.

Barnave’s early representative formation is placed under controversial figure89/95 and colonial policy101. The latter especially directs a reader seeking colonial policy rather than lawyer-deputy recruitment; the branch lacks an early-career cue. Mounier/province supply fallback, so partial rather than failed first lookup is appropriate.

Bordeaux commerce, institutions, Girondin/federalist politics and repression are distinct useful subtopics. The place entry does not label one as another; its omission of selectors makes repeated reading necessary. Port, institutional and political routes provide alternatives, so the proven path-level harm slows rather than blocks or misleads.

Brittany language/tenure, representation, federalism and religious resistance deserve separate selectors. Related Breton institutional and political entries partially relieve the burden, and the regional list itself remains inspectable. The remaining cause is localized scanning friction across these meanings, not loss of their source facts.

Catholic education, corporate rights, resistance and religious settlements are conflated in one selectable list. Adjacent Catholic Church, armies and orthodoxy routes help some inquiries. The broad adjective gives insufficient topical discrimination, but these source passages remain retrievable; no separate material false promise is demonstrated by this SUB finding.

Convention as governing assembly conceals constitutional, factional, war and emergency-policy choices in a long list. Its treaty sibling only separates a homonym, so meaningful selectors would reduce effort. Actual institution and subject routes still reach the treatments; the supported SUB consequence is slower selection rather than blocked access or an independently misleading claim.

Directory as government combines constitution, elections/coups and fiscal policy. Domestic/foreign and sister-republic alternatives provide some access even though they do not organize the main sequence. The cause established here is the extra work to select a policy topic within that sequence; no inaccessible topic or material false relation is established by subdivision evidence.

Europe interleaves reception, war, occupation and social/economic comparison. Country and thematic routes partly preserve retrieval, while the broad continent-first string forces additional reading. Cross-European selectors would improve efficiency, but the audited architecture has not been shown to block or materially mislead a particular inquiry.

France spans institutions, society, religion, war and foreign relations without selectors. Specific French compounds and topical headings retrieve portions, and all listed pages remain available. The broad route is cumbersome, but size and scanning expense alone do not establish a major cause. The independently supported consequence is repairable navigation friction.

II, Francis is an unnatural numeral-first inversion. It separates180/379 from Emperor Francis206/211 and Emperor Francis II206. A reader using Francis or Emperor Francis has no displayed direction to the additional numeral-filed pages. Propose minor HED for misleading filing/label order, one cause on this node; preserve actual locator source support.

The name entry supplies the relevant early pages under commander72 and opponent-of-Jacobins70, cues that indicate different requested activities and periods. Its politics74 branch gives the national-assembly demand but does not direct the reader to the earlier advisory role. Notables supplies fallback facts; the incompatible selection cues retain localized personal-sequence friction.

National is a standalone incomplete adjective with82displays/175assignments across distinct source noun phrases. Whole-path semantic uncertainty is already established; neither an omitted noun nor a universal nationalist concept may be invented. Physical evidence is inspectable, but promised subject and hence conceptual-subdivision prerequisites cannot be fixed honestly. Independently propose HED major for unusable label selection, while retaining this trigger as unresolved in private notes pending sanctioned representation. No full-mode completion attestation.
The path asserts National Guard activity outside France, but the audited destinations overwhelmingly concern forces within France or amalgamation into the army.
The post-Napoleonic-kingdom qualifier is absent from most destinations assigned to the path.

Political-order treatment is split between Old Regime and Ancien Régime > as political order (PATH-CCA6EEFD60C4:119134147157196219344) with no linking cross-reference. Current evidence distinguishes collapse/reorganization/restoration but the two synonymous labels do not communicate this split. One shared cause, not a second density defect.

Unaccented Orleans107 separates the duke from Orléans80,91,99,104,193 without a linking route. Consolidation or a reference would restore the connected personal sequence. Share cause with807, not two penalties. Orléans mixes the duke at80,91,99,104,193 with the city festival277; the bare heading gives no city/person distinction. Its unaccented duke variant107 is a separate fragmentation aspect. Current literal source support is not erased by ambiguity.

Paine, Thomas169 retrieves authorship/political defense; Paine, Tom194,285 retrieves Convention membership and restoration. Both identify the same person but neither name form directs to the other. Single cause shared with810.

Prussia in diplomacy and Prussians in diplomacy (PATH-DE6692327963) share201,302 but separate many other state-policy episodes. The noun-form distinction does not explain the partition and no cross-reference joins it. One cause shared with892.

Legal right118/421, judicial opposition37/75, religious refusal175, Federalist revolt238–249 and occupation resistance349–368 require distinct conceptual routes.54 displays span diverse actors, goals and geographical episodes. Existing named actors/events do not let a reader starting at Resistance select the intended type. Subdivision by target/form of resistance would be meaningful rather than arbitrary pagination; proposed SUB binding remains private.

Robespierre’s first political intervention95 is filed as Jacobin leader and lawyer-deputy101 as on justice. These cues imply mature leadership or legal views rather than early recruitment. Named pages are physically reachable and profession routes retrieve facts, so the earlier no is too strong; retain only localized partly successful first lookup.

The complete path presents Russia as revolutionary although all audited destinations describe monarchy, anti-revolution, coalition politics, or unrealized hopes.

Valid state-formation, national citizenship, French constitutional legitimacy and interstate sovereignty treatments are spread over59 display groups. These are substantively distinct questions even after removing false tokens. Organizing by formation/territorial sovereignty, representation/citizenship and national mobilization would let an umbrella reader select the relevant account; the present unqualified list does not. Proposed SUB remains a private finding and is not duplicated at the State parent.

United States combines the American republic66 with United States of Belgium163–164, whose full distinct heading also appears1108. The bare American conventional name gives no Belgian qualification; the clear full Belgian alternative reduces coverage risk but does not clarify this mixed heading to its reader.

Regnal numeral is alphabetized as V, William; the conventional William V of Orange route contains only75 while162/200/209/343/346–347 are stranded under V. No linking reference was found. The independently causal navigation problem is the inverted lookup name, not locator support.

Court/Assembly/popular-action subdivisions would be conceptual, while named-event routes alone do not guide readers entering at Versailles.

The complete path asserts a palace relationship that none of its audited destinations supports.
The path labels armies as insurgents, while most destinations concern regular, coalition, or revolutionary armies rather than insurgent forces.

Resolved treatments separate legitimacy theory, revolutionary sovereignty struggles, executive centralization, counter-revolutionary claims and exported authority.45 displayed groups leave those different questions undifferentiated under one temporal heading. Subdivision by holder/mechanism of authority would be conceptual. One unresolved49 locator does not affect the demonstrated distinction among the many resolved treatments; proposed SUB does not duplicate their precision exceptions.
The path conflates the legal-profession sense of bar with a physical barrier; none of its audited destinations supports the asserted sense.

Bishop singular is an undivided entry with political office75, Talleyrand132, Gobel261/271 and Liège162/164, whereas bishops plural splits church rulers, prince-bishops and revolution with different destinations. Number alone does not signal a conceptual separation and no linking reference exists. One shared consolidation/link cause, with no duplicate SUB penalty for the singular list.

Bourgeois > as social class22–24/27–29/91/94/224 and bourgeoisie > as social class22–25/27/48/90/93/394/407–408/423 share class identity but split distinct historical and concluding treatments without a link. Neither adjective/noun form indicates the division. One common variant-access cause; politics paths have the same complementary split.

Court as sovereign courts2/37/46/61/70/82 and courts as sovereign72/83 split the same institutional class without linking. Named parlements offer alternatives, so severity is minor navigation only; do not claim factual treatment absent or duplicate at1457.
The path mixes the princely-household sense of court with judicial courts; most destinations support the latter sense instead.

The displayed parent dauphin lacks the final accented é of Dauphiné, yet the child as province unequivocally identifies the province. This independent wrong-name presentation should be corrected to Dauphiné; all nine locators can remain supported because the qualifier recovers the intended geographic meaning. No lost factual coverage or duplicated locator penalty is claimed.
The path conflates territorial departments with government ministries and has no supported destination.

Social composition96–101/174/194, mandate independence117–118, legislative vulnerability228/274/278, mission powers227/237 and later institutional membership319/330/375 are separate representative-personnel questions.54 displays/11-page maximum require a reader starting at deputies to search through many unrelated legislative acts. The immunity subentry helps only one facet; selection, mandate and mission subdivisions would materially guide retrieval without merely splitting by page number. One SUB cause only.

Bare diet combines food/nutrition22 with Polish legislature165–166/207. Both meanings are valid source topics, but one unqualified label gives no distinction between unrelated senses. Add a food/legislature qualification or separate entry; this is an independent heading-selection/navigation issue, not a locator-support failure.

Executions254/275/278/282/300/326 contains distinct penal episodes absent from singular execution, with no linking reference. Number does not explain the split. Both routes should be consolidated or linked as one navigation cause; sentence/trial/person alternatives prevent automatic factual absence.
The historiography qualifier is not supported by any audited destination on the path.

CONFIRMED: The undivided law entry mixes local legal plurality2/4, constitutional/public law118–126, emergency economic controls246–265, repressive statutes251/275–278 and codification385/423. Meaningful legal-system, constitutional-rights, emergency-law and codification subheads would serve distinct inquiries. Existing maximum, hoarding and property entries rescue particular facts but do not provide a connected way to choose among these legal functions at law; the reader must scan a book-spanning undifferentiated run. This is navigation impairment, not factual coverage loss and not an extra penalty for wrong locators.
The path conflates ministry as a government department with cabinet or ministerial contexts and has no supported destination.

CONFIRMED: Paris in revolution combines constitutional relocation123, crowd/sectional power185–193, factional crises220–244, coercive institutions253–283, later unrest290–325 and consular politics374–390 without internal navigation. The existing market/culture/judicial/center siblings do not distinguish those revolutionary mechanisms; named events and actors rescue many facts but do not offer a usable capital-wide chronological or institutional choice at this entry. Conceptual phase/institution subheads would materially reduce searching across this exceptionally broad mixed narrative. No factual-access deduction is inferred and early temporal misassignments remain separate.

CONFIRMED: People combines economic livelihood/destitution14–30, monarchical audiences1, crowd action109–124, representative sovereignty193–196, coercion and resistance257–293, and later political/social consequences369–424. Social condition, collective action and sovereign people are substantively different reader questions. Poor, crowd, sovereignty and named episodes rescue facts but have no directing architecture from this aggregate entry; choosing a sense requires scanning a book-wide undivided list. Conceptual subheads would address this concrete ambiguity/search burden. This is independent navigation harm, not missed factual treatment or a count-based penalty.
The path mixes the noun 'poor' with incidental adjectival uses of 'inadequate'; most destinations do not treat poor people as inadequate.
The sole destination does not treat progress as an idea, leaving the access route unsupported.
The historiography qualifier fits only one of four destinations; the others discuss revolution directly rather than its interpretation.

The bare trial route interleaves ordinary procedure, the king's formal trial, Favras's rescue-plot prosecution and the Equals special court with many other defendants. Case/procedure subdivisions distinguish actual different inquiries, rather than slicing a continuous narrative. A reader starting with the legal proceeding cannot select the appropriate case from the unlabeled string. Trial by jury125 and trial in special courts27 cover particular procedure; named Babeuf and royal-person routes rescue individual facts but do not organize this legal-proceeding entry. This establishes substantial path-level scanning harm, not missing factual coverage for every bound subject.

Western guerrilla pacification315, legislative coercion375 and returning troops against brigandage384 answer different force-function questions. Their labels could be pacification, constitutional coups and civil policing, not arbitrary dates. The present domestic-order branch mixes these with crowd control and colonial enforcement, so its user must inspect unrelated functions. Hoche, Sieyes, local authorities and criminal courts provide positive alternatives to particular facts, but not an organized account of the requested domestic-force function. Billeting already has a sibling and is not proposed again. The harm is substantial scanning on this branch, not a denial of those alternatives or an inferred stance reversal.

American intervention/fiscal burden66–68, incompatible expectations producing war177–180 and conquest finance333 are independently required meanings, intermixed with campaign narratives, peace, occupation and retrospective consequences across the foreign-war branch. Named-conflict, diplomatic-purpose and financial-consequence subdivisions would let a war-first reader choose a real question before opening many unrelated passages. War-as-political-instrument, military-organization and transformative-force siblings help their own questions; they do not organize this branch's multi-conflict material. Positive State-finance and named diplomatic alternatives preserve benchmark coverage. Only the overloaded foreign-war starting route is charged.
